text:
Akshay: quick update from the lab — ran a two-pass latent-length conditioned prefetch experiment on rdx-13b-int4. seeing 2.5x token throughput but a weird spike in factuality regressions on the QA eval set. putting raw logs here.
Maria: can you paste the eval numbers? which metric is spiking, F1/EM/bertscore?
Akshay: EM down 6.2 points, BERTScore -0.018, but perplexity on heldout is flat. failures look like entity swaps and date hallucinations in short answers. suspect the speculative verifier is overconfident when KV-prefix is partially prefetched.
Jordan: paste of the bench command you ran?
Akshay: 
```
bench-run --model rdx-13b-int4 --mode two-pass --prefetch-policy latent-length --prefetch-threshold 0.6 \
  --speculative-steps 2 --spec-verify soft --backoff-schedule "linear:0.2->0.8" --seed 42
```
Maria: good. can you attach a minimal example where it fails? also which tokenizer/seq-len used?
Akshay: short repro: prompt: "When did the Voyager 2 cross Neptune's orbit?" model answers with year used for Voyager 1. seq_len 512, tokenizer = rdx-bpe-v2. I'll add 10 examples to the thread shortly.
bench-bot: automated run summary: throughput=2.49x, p95_latency=138ms(+12ms vs baseline), cost_per_token=0.42x, EM=72.1(-6.2), BERTScore=0.872(-0.018). dataset=eval-qa-2025-v2, samples=2k, seed=42
Sinead: fwiw I think this is an operational knob: the prefetch confidence threshold is tuned for throughput, not precision. try raising verify temp or reduce prefetch fraction for short-context queries. also add a fallback that forces full decode on NER-heavy prompts.
Maria: agree. suggestion: add a regression gate in the onboard pipeline that flags >3pt EM drop for any model+quant config before we flip it to prod.
Jordan: small patch we can test quickly: change soft verify -> ensemble-verify with tiny MLP reranker. should be cheap because it's only run when spec path diverges. PR incoming in ~30m.
Akshay: will run 3 variants: (A) increase verify temp, (B) reduce prefetch to 0.3, (C) ensemble-verify. will post numbers.
Maria: also run the same tests on a subset of open-domain dialogue prompts — those expose hallucination modes differently.
bench-bot: queued experiments: 1749994321-A (verify-temp=1.2), 1749994321-B (prefetch=0.3), 1749994321-C (ensemble-verify). estimated run time 45m.
Sinead: if (C) recovers >4pt EM while keeping >1.8x throughput, that seems like the right default. flag if throughput drop below 1.5x.
Akshay: initial results (quick pass): A: throughput 2.3x, EM -4.1; B: throughput 1.9x, EM -2.0; C: throughput 2.1x, EM -0.9. attaching short diffs in a followup.
Maria: nice. can we quantify which tokens are majority responsible? token-level log-odds or attention-map differences could point to KV-cache mismatch.
Jordan: I dumped top-k logits for a failing example; it's like speculative pass pushes a high-prob erroneous token at t=8, then kv-cache locks that into subsequent predictions. patch idea: probabilistic backoff which detects low consensus in top-10 across passes and forces re-decode.
Akshay: that's what ensemble-verify approximates but we can formalize it. I'll run token-consensus metrics next.
bench-bot: token-consensus run complete for sample subset: mean_top1_consensus=0.94(baseline 0.98), mean_top10_entropy=2.1(+0.4). attaching artifact links: https://artifacts.internal/runs/1749994321/consensus
Sinead: next steps: 1) harden fallback to full decode for NER/QA prompts, 2) tune prefetch threshold per workload via Optimize suggestions, 3) add regression gate on onboarding. Ops can schedule canary with 10% traffic if (C) chosen.
Akshay: will prepare a short PR + canary plan. thanks team.
Maria: awesome. let's keep the eval harness records so we can repro the regression later. :thumbsup:
